prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority.Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline. Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages.Business Rules Registry governs fairness,spacing,subscriptions,runway-specific queue thresholds.Cedarbell normalizes Airport Capacity Plan;Marlinstone predicts demand;Capacity Assessment Module compares Airport Acceptance Rate/runway/taxiway/sector limits.Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;runway/fix/Ground Delay Program constraints;capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory.Halcyon confirms publication,requests delay/fairness adjustments,checks Slot Compliance State.Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:advisory movements/timestamped milestones.Quartzline sends Stand Tow Request Form;Blueharbor recalculates.Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities;Lantern distributes approvals.Saffron shall confirm revisions before freeze-horizon;justified connection/crew/rotation reviews. Quartzline verifies queue-card pad-entry order before staging movement authorization;must coordinate every pad release with Brindle.Emberline withholds push clearances above safe holding capacity until below configured threshold.Ironleaf reserves positions only with achievable pad-release time/valid runway taxi path.Foxglove records fluid type/mixture/start/completion/holdover

New part:
S394: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares planned treatment throughput, actual pad occupancy, and departure compliance to improve winter capacity assumptions for future events.
S395: Arrival regulation begins when the Demand Prediction Service shows that inbound demand will exceed the Airport Acceptance Rate within the planning horizon.
S396: The Regional Flow Manager evaluates regulation options in the Arrival Regulation Console using runway availability, sector load, stand readiness, and forecast weather as the controlling inputs.
S397: The preferred option in Normal Operations is a minor time-based sequence adjustment that moves delay to upstream departure points rather than to airborne holding near Meridian.
S398: When the imbalance is larger, the Slot Allocation Engine can support a Ground Delay Program that meters selected arrivals before they depart for the region.
S399: The Regional Flow Manager uses the restriction notice to bound the arrival regulation timeline before committing new landing-rate values in the Arrival Regulation Console.
S400: The Capacity Assessment Module calculates candidate Airport Acceptance Rate values for each runway configuration and exposes the operational basis for each value on the Common Situation Display.
S401: The Tower Supervisor confirms whether the proposed landing rate is compatible with runway occupancy, missed approach protection, and local spacing constraints.
S402: The Airspace Sector Planner confirms whether terminal and en-route sector loads can absorb the regulated stream without generating unsafe compression.
S403: The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews the proposed treatment for network impact and identifies flights where upstream delay would create a disproportionate connection or aircraft rotation penalty.
S404: The Slot Coordinator then uses the Slot Allocation Engine to distribute arrival times according to the approved business rules and any protected flight criteria in the Business Rules Registry.
S405: The Airport CDM Portal presents the resulting arrival plan to Aircraft Operator Representative users and records acknowledgements in the Collaborative Decision Log.
S406: Airborne holding prevention is the primary design objective because excess holding increases fuel burn, controller workload, and the likelihood of unplanned diversion.
S407: The Arrival Regulation Console therefore issues alerts before predicted holding stacks form, not after airborne delay has already accumulated.
S408: The Sector Load Monitor contributes early warnings when converging arrival flows are projected to exceed terminal sector capacity under the current metering plan.
S409: The Weather Ingest Gateway updates the arrival model when wind shifts, visibility reductions, or convective activity change achievable runway throughput.
S410: If weather or runway conditions degrade faster than the model forecast, the Regional Flow Manager may apply a tactical landing-rate reduction for a defined review interval.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
